docs.title: Annie Paige
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Archaeologist / Explorer Location: Seattle → Green River Gorge → Bone King's cabin Faction: Independent Status: Alive (recurring)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Short brown hair, khaki pants, yellow top, blue scarf. Pith helmet. Carries an archaeology kit and a Colt Rainmaker. Usually slightly drunk when first encountered. Looks younger than she is.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Born in Massachusetts. Worked with her father in archaeology from childhood. Educated at Oxford. Royal Geographic Society membership recently revoked — she's furious about it and will tell you why at length, whether you asked or not.

Has a Necronomicon skull fragment in her bag. Believes she found proof of alien structures at Cahokia. Nobody believes her. She may be right.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: Prove everyone who doubted her wrong. Find the thing that can't exist. She's brilliant and chaotic and impossible to stop once she's locked onto something.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Loud. Funny. Incapable of leaving anything alone. Gets drunk and overshares classified archaeological secrets. Completely fearless in the way that only people who haven't fully processed their own mortality are.

docs.title: Stat Block
docs.text: Attributes: Agility d6, Smarts d8, Spirit d8, Strength d6, Vigor d6 Skills: Academics d8, Athletics d6, Common Knowledge d6, Fighting d4, Healing d4, Notice d6, Persuasion d4, Science d4, Shooting d6, Stealth d4 Pace: 6 | Parry: 4 | Toughness: 5 Edges: Brave Hindrances: Curious Gear: Pith helmet, archaeology kit, Colt Rainmaker (Range 12/24/48, Damage 2d6, AP 1)

docs.title: Key Connections
docs.text:
• Dr. Mary Ann Connor (Territory University) — knows Annie and considers her "preposterous" theories about Viking habitation outrageous. Annie considers the feeling mutual.
  • Muckleshoot Territory — Annie's Viking site is in or near sacred Muckleshoot land; the tribe has asked for help turning her away (see The Draugr, p.88)

docs.title: Appearances in Campaign
docs.text:
1. Little Annie Orphaned (book p.65) — met in a saloon, drunk, recently expelled from RGS
  2. The Draugr (book p.88) — at the Green River Gorge, insists on going in
  3. The Bone King (book p.122) — at Yashulid's cabin

docs.title: Deputy Chandra Lawson
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Deputy Sheriff, Seattle Location: Seattle Faction: Law Status: Alive (recurring)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The almost always cheery Deputy hails from Kansas with a thick country accent — and an occasional Haitian influence she picked up from her "grams," the same woman who taught her voodoo. Curious to a fault. Asks detailed questions about the party's investigations, how they defeated some creature, what ammo they used. She's genuinely their best friend if they let her be. Carries a Colt Lightning and a club.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: Keep Seattle safe. She's good at this job and she knows it. Doesn't need help — but she'll take it when offered, which puts the party in a complicated position of being useful and unofficial.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Direct. Dry. Loyal to people who prove they deserve it. Will tell you exactly what she thinks and what she can and cannot do, and won't apologize for either.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Mother was a slave in Louisiana who learned voodoo from her own mother. Chandra keeps this quiet, but uses it when it helps crack a case. She's pushing for the title of "Assistant Chief of Police" but Woolery hasn't agreed yet.

She's a member of the Twilight Legion — which the party may or may not know depending on how that introduction unfolds.

docs.title: Role in Campaign
docs.text:
• Party's primary law enforcement contact
  • Bridge between official Seattle and the weird
  • Complained to by women whose husbands visit Red Line Insurance and come home "changed" — a clue toward Bloodsucking Fiends
  • Act Three: Captured by howlers; appears as a simulacrum created by the Bone King at the edge of his domain (legless, cheerfully warning the party to turn back)
  • Recurs throughout all three Acts; named as a potential "victim" in the Bone King's trials

docs.title: Giuseppe Marinetti
docs.text: [!info] NPC Head cook at the Grand Central Hotel. Part of Seattle's Italian community. Reliable, discreet, and willing to go out of his way for someone who has earned his trust.

docs.title: Character Notes
docs.text: A practical man. Good with food, better with favours. Part of the Italian community network that now owes Father Miller a debt after the Vivaldi resolution. Currently occupied with private research.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: Character Notes Father Thomas Miller Trusted — asked by him to research Salish elk mythology Jerome Bianchi Works under him at the Grand Central Italian Community Member, connected

docs.title: Active Thread
docs.text: Elk Mythology Research — Father Miller asked Marinetti to look into Salish mythology around elk. He is still working on it. Not ready to share results. The Telegraph Context notes 1 exchange has been used on this thread; 1 remains before a natural pause.

docs.title: GM Notes

docs.title: H.P. Lovelace
docs.text: [!info] NPC — Player Created An in-world author of horror and romance fiction, based in Providence, Rhode Island. Created by Stalker Jack (Mama Duvall's player) as part of Mama Duvall's backstory. Mama Duvall reads his work extensively.

docs.title: Character Notes
docs.text: A writer of dark, atmospheric fiction. Health uncertain. Signs correspondence simply as "Lovelace, Providence." Replies are brief, formal, and slightly ominous in tone — the pen of a man who lives too close to whatever he writes about.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: Character Notes Mama Duvall Fan and correspondent. Lovelace received her message warmly.

docs.title: Telegraph Exchange — 2026-04-26
docs.text:
Mama Duvall sent: Fan message praising his work and wishing him good health; hoping his next novel is not far away.

Response: MAMA DE VALL SEATTLE STOP YOUR KIND WORDS RECEIVED WITH GREAT PLEASURE STOP THE DARK MUSES ARE RESTLESS AND THE NEXT TALE STIRS IN THE SHADOWS STOP HEALTH UNCERTAIN BUT THE PEN DOES NOT REST STOP PROVIDENCE WATCHES OVER US ALL STOP LOVELACE PROVIDENCE RHODE ISLAND STOP

docs.title: GM Notes
docs.text:
• Pure character development — no plot relevance. Bot can handle freely.
  • If Mama Duvall writes again, Lovelace can respond in this voice: world-weary, literary, slightly gothic.
  • Keep him in Providence — no reason for him to come west.

docs.title: Horace Clayton
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Reporter, Seattle Post-Intelligencer Location: Seattle — his beat is the whole city Faction: The Press Status: Alive (recurring)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Wiry. Always has a notebook. Never quite seems to be paying attention and always is. Drinks moderately. Remembers everything.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Has been covering Seattle since before it was worth covering. Knows where most bodies are buried — figuratively. A few literally, after the last few weeks.

Works under Editor Thomas Prosch and Owner Leigh Hunt at the Post-Intelligencer.

docs.title: Voice
docs.text:
Dry wit. Victorian propriety with a raised eyebrow underneath it. Prints the official line but includes details that make the reader think. Never lies — just selects. Will describe a supernatural event in language that sounds mundane while including every detail that makes it obviously not.

"The conductor maintains it was merely a freak bush leaping from the tracks in the dead of night."

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: The truth. But more practically, a good story. He's not reckless — he won't print something that gets someone killed. But he's watching everything and writing it all down somewhere.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Professionally warm. Remembers your name, your drink, what you said three weeks ago. Asks questions that sound like small talk. Will absolutely print the thing you said off the record if it's interesting enough and you didn't say "off the record" first.

docs.title: Background (from Book)
docs.text:
Seattle's first African American journalist. Covers politics and occasionally stranger stories. A trusted ally of Tombstone Epitaph reporter Lacy O'Malley.

Works under Editor Thomas Prosch (taciturn; only interested in facts; at odds with Clayton's instincts but defers to ownership) and Owner Leigh Hunt (bullish on sharing information and revealing truth; frequent thorn in the Agency's side).

Agent Tatum Black works with Clayton occasionally — helping him find the line between reporting the truth and sending the public into an outright panic.

The Post-Intelligencer building is on the northeast corner of Yesler Way and Post Street.

docs.title: Role in Campaign
docs.text:
• Primary in-world narrator voice
  • Party's interface with the public perception of their actions
  • Quietly accumulating information the party doesn't know he has
  • Will become more significant if the party cultivates or burns the relationship

docs.title: Jerome Bianchi
docs.text: [!info] At a Glance Role: Hotel Manager, Grand Central Hotel Location: Grand Central Hotel, Seattle Faction: Civilian Status: Alive

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Compact, professional Italian-American man. Well-dressed, precise. Has managed the Grand Central for eleven years. Radiates practiced calm and professional hospitality.

docs.title: Background
docs.text: Born to Italian immigrants. Grandmother from Naples — he speaks Italian fluently. Has managed the Grand Central since 1873. Was aware of the haunting by Giuseppe Vivaldi for years but kept it quiet to protect the hotel's reputation.

docs.title: Motivation
docs.text: Protect the hotel. Protect its reputation. Keep things running smoothly. He's not a bad man — just a pragmatic one.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text: Deflects with hospitality. Offers food when things get uncomfortable. Not dishonest exactly — just extremely selective about what he volunteers. Warms up considerably once he trusts someone.

docs.title: Staff
docs.text:
• Camille Broad — assistant manager; helps watch the desk and keep the books
  • Giuseppe Marinetti — hotel cook; researching Salish elk mythology at the Priest's request
  • Half-dozen maintenance staff and maids

docs.title: Stat Block
docs.text: Uses Citizen profile (p.129) with the following adjustments: Hindrances: Doubting Thomas, Loyal Trade (Business): d8 He backs down quickly from confrontation. Will not allow wall demolition without Persuasion –2 or distraction.

docs.title: Key Interactions
docs.text:

  • Will not allow wall demolition without Persuasion –2 or distraction

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A secret organisation operating across the West, dedicated to investigating and suppressing supernatural threats. Operatives work independently in the field; the Legion provides resources, intelligence, and backup when justified.

docs.title: Contacting the Legion
docs.text:
The party can send requests to the Legion via telegraph. Responses come from a regional handler — a Legion coordinator based in the Pacific Northwest. Tone: terse, professional, cautious. The Legion does not waste words and does not commit resources without justification.

Handler telegraph identity: LEGION NORTHWEST RELAY

docs.title: What the Legion Can Provide
docs.text: Resource Availability Notes Intelligence Case-by-case Information on known threats, entities, or persons of interest Backup Requires justification Field operatives; not dispatched lightly Equipment Requires requisition Specialised gear for supernatural threats Extraction Emergency only Getting a compromised operative out Authorisation GM decision Formal backing for sensitive operations

docs.title: GM Notes
docs.text:
• NPC membership is forbidden territory for the bot. If a player asks whether a specific NPC is Legion, the handler deflects: "Operational security. That information is not transmitted by wire."
  • Use Legion responses to give the party direction without railroading — hints, not orders.
  • Legion requests that touch on main plot content (Bone King, Fear Machine, etc.) should be flagged to #marshal-desk for GM response rather than bot-generated.

docs.title: Small Animal Ghosts
docs.text: Session: 3 Status: Active

docs.title: What Mama Duvall Knows
docs.text:
Following the Sack-Headed Man encounter, Mama Duvall befriended a coterie of small animal ghosts. They are loyal to her specifically.

Capabilities: - Scout ahead — small, unnoticed - Report observations back to Mama Duvall - Minor interference — small sounds, knocking things over, brief distractions

Limitations: - Cannot fight - Cannot interact with the physical world beyond minor interference - Loyal to Mama Duvall only — not transferable

docs.title: The Batsquatch
docs.text: Session: 6 — November 3, 1884 Status: Resolved

docs.title: What Happened
docs.text:
Five devil bats — including a Devil Bat Queen locally nicknamed "Batsquatch" — had roosted atop the Yesler-Leery Building and were hunting lone pedestrians in the fog. Not a sasquatch. The party accessed the rooftop and dealt with the threat.

During the encounter a fire broke out and Mama Duvall put it out — destroying Jim's hat in the process.

docs.title: Loot
docs.text: Recovered from the aerie: victim belongings (watches, jewelry), sailor's scrimshaw piece.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
• Threat eliminated
  • Party gave interview to Horace Clayton → November 3rd Post-Intelligencer edition
  • Jim's hat: destroyed. Mama Duvall is responsible. This continues.

docs.title: GM Notes
docs.text:
• The scrimshaw piece: assign a hook or value if needed
  • Horace Clayton now has Father Miller on record as dreaming of elk (mentioned in interview)

docs.text: Session: 5 Status: Active — unexplained

docs.title: What the Characters Know
docs.text: Both Father Thomas Miller and Mama Duvall chipped a tooth on the same day during Session 5. No explanation has been established. Neither character knows the connection.

docs.title: The Forgotten Train
docs.text: [!warning] Open Mystery Active. The party has no memory of this event.

docs.title: What Is Known (Marshal Only)
docs.text:
The inbound express that arrived October 20th, 1884 — the party's arrival train — had something happen to it. The third passenger car showed strange jagged scorch marks on the exterior, metal buckled as if exposed to a blacksmith's forge.

The conductor attributed it to a freak bush leaping from the tracks. This is not true.

The party (Jim, Mama Duvall, and whatever other passengers were aboard) has no memory of the incident.

docs.title: What Horace Clayton Knows
docs.text: He printed a sidebar in the Oct 22 edition. He noted: - The scorch marks were on the third passenger car specifically - The metal was buckled as if from extreme heat - The conductor's explanation was implausible - The article cut off mid-sentence in his notes — something interrupted him

docs.title: Evidence That Exists In The World
docs.text:
• The scorch marks on the train car (if it's still in the yard)
  • Other passengers who were on that train
  • The conductor (who is lying or was instructed to lie)
  • Possibly: physical marks, objects, or symptoms the party carries unknowingly

docs.title: What Actually Happened
docs.text: (Fill this in when you decide — leave blank until ready)

docs.title: Distinction From The Vampire Train
docs.text:
Forgotten Train Vampire Train Date Oct 20, 1884 — recent Earlier — historical Who Jim, Mama Duvall, party Mama Duvall (alone) Memory Lost — nobody remembers Remembered via flashback Status Active mystery Character backstory Connection Unknown Possibly Mama Duvall's Harrowing

These are two separate incidents. The confusion is understandable given the setting.

docs.title: Possible Payoff Moments
docs.text:
• Party finds the train car still in the rail yard — the scorch marks are still there
  • Another passenger recognises them and remembers something they don't
  • A recovered object from that night surfaces
  • The conductor is found and interrogated
  • Someone or something that was on that train comes looking for them

docs.title: The Haunted Hotel
docs.text: Session: 5 — Late October, 1884 Status: Resolved

docs.title: What Happened
docs.text:
The Grand Central Hotel was haunted by the spirit of Giuseppe Vivaldi, a carpenter who died entombed in the hotel walls during its construction in 1880. Not evil — driven mad by decades of imprisonment. The party tracked him through the building (Room 313, the north wall, the basement furnace), demolished the bricked-up wall, and returned his toolbelt to his family.

Jerome Bianchi resisted demolition but was ultimately persuaded. Giuseppe's spirit is at rest.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
• Ghost laid to rest
  • Family received Vivaldi's toolbelt
  • Party acquired Vivaldi's Timepiece (relic — powers TBC from boxed set card)
  • Father Miller gains the aid of Seattle's Italian community
  • Jerome Bianchi now a friendly, quietly grateful contact

docs.title: GM Notes
docs.text:
• Vivaldi's Timepiece: check boxed set card for mechanical effects
  • The Italian community favour is active — Father Miller can call on them

docs.title: The Priest — Father Thomas Miller
docs.text:
[!tip] Player Character Full Name: Father Thomas Miller Player: Paul Waggott Religion: Catholic Status: Alive Harrowed: No

"The Priest" is the GM/wiki alias. He is known publicly as "the Reverend Father." His telegraph identity is Father Thomas Miller.

docs.title: Player Notes
docs.text:
Submitted by Paul Waggott via Telegraph Office, 2026-04-26

Father Thomas Miller is a Catholic Priest, specialising in exorcisms and the eternal war with the forces of hell. He is in his late 40s, 6' tall, with black hair. He originally hails from the Boston area, and studied in Rome. He is a member of The Twilight Legion.

docs.title: Character Overview
docs.text: A Catholic priest operating in the Pacific Northwest. Devout. Practical about the supernatural in a way that probably unsettles his superiors back east. Has seen enough in Seattle to reframe his theology considerably.

docs.title: Physical
docs.text:
Late 40s. 6 feet tall. Black hair. Originally from Boston. Studied theology in Rome. Carries himself with the quiet authority of a man who has seen worse things than whatever is currently happening and survived them all.

Submitted by Paul Waggott via Telegraph Office, 2026-04-26.

docs.text: Old cowboy type. Arrived with Mama Duvall on the October 20th express. Veteran of enough to be unimpressed by most things. Apparently including cardiac episodes.
